Dilapidation Survey

Protect yourself before construction starts next door.

6 photosCommercial & Asset

Before construction or demolition works begin nearby, a dilapidation survey records the existing condition of your property. If damage occurs later, you have dated, professional evidence of the original condition — critical for claims.

What's included

  • Pre-construction condition recording
  • Existing crack & defect mapping with photos
  • Dated documentation for legal reference
  • Post-construction comparison survey (optional)
  • Support for damage claims

What you receive

  • Dated condition report
  • Photo-mapped crack register
  • Evidence usable in disputes

Why It Matters

Prove What Was Already There — and What Wasn't

Dated Pre-Construction Record

Timestamped, professional evidence of exactly how your property was before works

Crack Mapping with Measurements

Every existing crack located, measured and photographed — not just described

Protection for Both Sides

Owners prove new damage; contractors disprove false claims — the record is neutral

Post-Construction Comparison

We return after works and compare item by item against the original record

Support for Damage Claims

Clear before-and-after evidence to support a claim against the responsible party

Prepared by a Registered Surveyor

A RISM-registered professional's record carries weight in negotiation and proceedings

How It Works

4 Stages of a Dilapidation Survey

Timing is everything — the record must exist before the works begin

1

Engaged Before Works Start

Contact us as soon as you learn of nearby construction, demolition or piling

2

Pre-Construction Survey

We record the existing condition in full — every crack located, measured and dated

3

Post-Construction Survey

After the works, we re-survey the same items using the same method and positions

4

Comparison & Claim Support

Side-by-side comparison identifies new damage — and supports your claim if there is any
